_README: REVIEW-TRIGGER list, not a permission list -- same rule as DEFAULT_WATCHLIST
in trust_runtime.py. A match here never grants access by itself.
ENGLISH-ONLY BY DESIGN: every term and alias in this file is an
ASCII/Latin transliteration, even for manufacturers whose native
branding is in Cyrillic (e.g. Kamaz, Belaz, Rusak). No native-script
text is stored anywhere in this file -- keys, aliases, or notes.
TRADE-OFF: this means a prompt/asset name written in actual Cyrillic
(e.g. the real Cyrillic spelling of Kamaz) will NOT be caught by
TrustRuntime._normalize()'s substring match against these entries,
since matching is literal-substring, not phonetic. If your project
generates or ingests Russian-language prompts/asset names, this is a
real coverage gap, not a cosmetic one -- consider a separate,
explicitly-scoped multi-script alias module if that matters for your
pipeline, rather than silently assuming transliteration is sufficient.
Legal basis: TRADEMARK on the manufacturer/model name, and -- for
several of these, especially the passenger-car and heavy-equipment
entries -- vehicle body designs are also frequently protected as trade
dress or registered design/industrial-design rights in various
jurisdictions, independent of the name. There is no known Epic IP
Partner Licensing Agreement pathway for any vehicle manufacturer as of
2026-08-02 (that program covers entertainment franchises like LEGO/
TMNT/Star Wars, not automakers). Matching a term here should resolve
to BLOCKED unless your studio holds a real, independently-negotiated
license from that specific manufacturer
(license_type='creator_independent_license' in license_manifest.json)
-- e.g. a genuine licensed racing/sim partnership. Never add a
manifest entry because a deal 'seems plausible.'
SCOPE LIMIT (read before relying on this for a vehicle-heavy build):
this is a text-match gate over tool-call payloads. It only catches the
manufacturer/model NAME appearing in a prompt, asset label, or code
string. It cannot detect a mesh that visually replicates a real
vehicle's body/silhouette (e.g. a BMW kidney grille, a Peterbilt hood
shape) without the name ever appearing in text -- trade dress risk from
pure geometry is a separate, unsolved problem this file does not cover.
HIGH FALSE-POSITIVE RISK: several brand names in this list transliterate
to, or resemble, ordinary dictionary words (e.g. the manufacturer 'Sever'
is the Russian word for 'north'; 'Gaz' collides with the English word
'gas'; 'Khan' is a common name/title; 'Zvezda' is the Russian word for
'star'; 'Sokol' is the Russian word for 'falcon'). These are flagged
'false_positive_risk': 'high' and are NOT included in the flattened
term list by default -- see 'enabled': false. Enable them only with a
qualifying alias (e.g. a specific model name) after checking your own
audit log for noise, exactly as trust_runtime.py's _normalize()
docstring warns for blunt substring matching in general.
Sourced from the manufacturer/model list supplied 2026-08-02, covering:
wheeled amphibious all-terrain vehicles, articulated/multi-axle
vehicles, tracked ATVs, giant quads, air boats, long-haul trucks,
construction/heavy equipment, passenger cars, and extreme special-
purpose transport (military/rescue/mining).
